what_i_see: Compact red (orange in H/Y/VIS) early-type-looking core with a bluer, knotty arc about 1 arcsec to its south, curving around the core over roughly 120 degrees and concave toward it; a fainter diffuse extension toward the west/north-west. Arc is distinct in VIS soft and hard stretches.
most_likely: Galaxy-scale strong-lens candidate: red deflector with a lensed blue background arc, Einstein radius near 1 arcsec. A ring or tidal feature around a single galaxy remains plausible.
against_it: No counter-image clearly seen on the north side; the arc is knotty and could be a star-forming ring, tidal arm or chance-aligned companion. Low S/N; no redshifts.
decisive_test: Lens modelling of the VIS cutout for a counter-image, then spectroscopy showing the arc at higher redshift than the red core (two distinct redshifts).
catalogue_notes: AllWISE J093605.73+735720.9 at 0.65" (W1 16.94, W1-W2 0.34, galaxy-like). NED: only WISE/2MASS sources; NVSS J093604+735800 at ~39". SIMBAD: nothing within 2'. Gaia DR3: nothing within 21". PS1: no row within 4". Lens/cluster catalogues not successfully queried.
